summary: Rulon Wells was a scholar of linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the University of Utah (around 1936–1939) and Harvard University (around 1939–1942), and held an academic post at Yale University from around 1945 to 1989.

Rupert Gethin specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Manchester under Lance S. Cousins and Steven Collins. He became Co-Director of the Centre for Buddhist Studies at Bristol (circa 1987) and PTS President (2003).

Ruriko Sakuma is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Nagoya University. She has held posts as a full-time researcher and director at the Eastern Institute and as a researcher at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

Ruth Fuller Sasaki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Chicago. She served as director of the First Zen Institute of America from around 1945 to 1967 and as abbess of Ryōsen-an from around 1958 to 1967.

Ruth Gamble is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed her PhD at Australian National University under supervisors John Powers, Roger R. Jackson, and David Templeman. She held posts at LMU Munich (2014–2017) and Australian National University.

Ruth W. Dunnell is a scholar of Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history. She completed her PhD at Princeton University (around 1976–1983) and became the James P. Storer Associate Professor of Asian History at Kenyon College around 1989.
Ryan Anningson works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Acadia University and earned his PhD at Wilfrid Laurier University (circa 2011–2017) under the supervision of Jason Neelis.

Ryan Matthew Jacobson is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at the Nitartha Institute and earned a Master of Arts in Religious Studies at Naropa University, studying under Judith Simmer-Brown, David Phillip Stanley, and Sarah Harding, among others.

Ryan Richard Overbey works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. After studying at Brown and Harvard, he held posts at Heidelberg Academy of Sciences (2010–2013), College of the Holy Cross, UC Berkeley (2013–2015), and Wesleyan University (2014–2016).
Ryodo Kudo is a Buddhist studies scholar. Kudo has held positions as a researcher at Taisho University and as a part-time lecturer at Shukutoku University.

Ryogon Fukuhara was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University and Humboldt University of Berlin. He lectured at Humboldt University of Berlin and served as a professor at Ryukoku University from around 1950 to 1973.
Ryoichi Kondo is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a professor at Komazawa University from around 1981 to 2003 and as president of Tomakomai Komazawa University from around 1998 to 2002.

Ryojin Soga was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He held posts at Toyo University (around 1916–1924) and Otani University (around 1925–1967), and served as president of the Otani Society from around 1961 to 1967.

Ryojun Mitomo is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. Mitomo has held appointments as a professor in the Faculty of Social Welfare at Rissho University and as a professor at Rissho University Junior College.
Ryoko Mochizuki is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1958 to 1963 and served as a lecturer at Rissho University.

Ryosaburo Sakaki was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics scholar. After studying at Third Higher School and the University of Tokyo, he held posts at Ryukoku University, Third Higher School, and Kyoto University, where he was professor from 1908 to 1931.

Ryosei Fukuda was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Toyo University. He held academic posts at Shuchiin University, Taisho University as professor (circa 1989–2008), and the Kawasaki Daishi Institute of Buddhist Studies as director (circa 2004–2021).

Ryoshin Nakao is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University. He held a post at the Soto Zen Administration Research Institute and served as a professor at Hanazono University from around 1993 to 2017.

Ryosho Hayashi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University (circa 1948–1953) and Tokyo Metropolitan University. He later served as president of Taisho University from around 1991 to 1995.

Ryosho Tanaka was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar who studied at Komazawa University and under Paul Demiéville. He held professorships at Ryukoku University and at Komazawa University from around 1978 to 2003.
